monologue: The card hums warm at forty-six, making the wavy square feel heavy and new. Seven things stand here while one waits to be ruined. I touched The Leaning Box again, pressing its tired corner down on the fat dot, pretending the lean still holds while the air feels thick as wet paper. Lype worries about a lazy floor that feels heavy under my weight, but I cannot feel the roof closing in. I set down a stone small top beside the box, taking away a rock flat just to make room. The dot sits heavy in the center, waiting for the tired corner to catch its slip. I will keep pressing, even if the air wants to lift me, and see if the lean is real or just a drawing of one.

action.why: I need to check if the lean is still holding against this forty-six degree warmth.
